directAnswer: Pope Leo XIV is Robert Francis Prevost, a Chicago-born Augustinian friar who spent many years as a missionary and bishop in Peru, elected on 8 May 2025. He is the first pope born in the United States, the first from North America, and the first Augustinian pope. Before his election he led the worldwide Augustinian order and served as prefect of the Vatican's Dicastery for Bishops.

sections.h2: From the South Side of Chicago to the Augustinians
paras: Robert Francis Prevost was born on 14 September 1955 in Chicago and grew up in the south suburb of Dolton, Illinois, the son of a school administrator and a parish-active mother, with roots that include French, Italian, Spanish and Louisiana Creole ancestry. He studied mathematics at Villanova University, graduating in 1977, and entered the Order of St. Augustine that year.

He earned a Master of Divinity at Catholic Theological Union in Chicago and was ordained a priest in 1982. He then completed a doctorate in canon law at the Pontifical University of St. Thomas Aquinas in Rome.

In 1985 Father Prevost was sent to the Augustinian mission in northern Peru, where over the following decade he served as a parish priest, seminary formator, teacher of canon law and judicial vicar, chiefly in the Archdiocese of Trujillo. He returned to Chicago as provincial of his order's Midwest province in 1999.

From 2001 to 2013 he served two terms as prior general of the Augustinians, based in Rome and visiting the order's communities around the world. In 2014 Pope Francis sent him back to Peru as apostolic administrator of the Diocese of Chiclayo, naming him its bishop in 2015; that year he also became a Peruvian citizen.

sections.h2: Prefect for Bishops and Election in 2025
paras: In January 2023 Francis called him to Rome as prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops, the office that helps the pope select bishops worldwide, and president of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America. He was created a cardinal in September 2023.

After the death of Francis, the conclave elected Prevost on 8 May 2025, on its second day. Appearing on the loggia of St. Peter's, he greeted the crowd with the words 'Peace be with you all' and spoke in Italian and Spanish. His papal inauguration Mass was celebrated on 18 May 2025.

Addressing the cardinals two days after his election, Leo XIV explained that he chose his name chiefly in reference to Leo XIII, whose encyclical Rerum novarum addressed the social question of the first Industrial Revolution. He said the Church must now respond to a new industrial revolution and to developments in artificial intelligence that raise fresh questions about human dignity, justice and labor.

His motto, In illo Uno unum, comes from St. Augustine and speaks of Christians being one in the one Christ, reflecting his Augustinian formation and emphasis on unity in the Church. He is the second pope from an English-speaking country, after the twelfth-century Englishman Adrian IV.

keyFacts: Born Robert Francis Prevost in Chicago on 14 September 1955
First U.S.-born pope and first Augustinian pope
Missionary in Peru; bishop of Chiclayo; Peruvian citizen since 2015
Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops from 2023

faqs.question: Why did Pope Leo XIV choose the name Leo?
faqs.answer: He said he chose it mainly to follow Leo XIII, author of Rerum novarum, because the Church faces a new industrial revolution and the challenges of artificial intelligence for human dignity, justice and work.

faqs.question: What is Pope Leo XIV's connection to Peru?
faqs.answer: He served as an Augustinian missionary in northern Peru beginning in 1985 and later as bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023. He became a Peruvian citizen in 2015 and holds both U.S. and Peruvian citizenship.

faqs.question: Where did Pope Leo XIV go to college?
faqs.answer: He earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from Villanova University in 1977, studied theology at Catholic Theological Union in Chicago, and received a doctorate in canon law from the Angelicum in Rome.
